images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — where the 16 openings at 4 ft height are (lift lobby enclosure test)
images.explanation: Plan of Building 9 Floor 0.5 cut at 4 ft, with the lift pins 115/116 (red stars) and the enclosure probe. Each numbered red circle is one of the 16 places where the lobby enclosure test leaks; each was confirmed necessary by removing only that diagnostic closure and retesting. Only #1 (63.5 mm, q1a) and #2 (11.9 mm, q1c) are openings you could see at drawing scale. #7 is the place reported as the '50 mm gap' (q1b); the evidence shows the 50 mm is filled by a mullion and the real leak there is a 1.6 µm hairline. The other 13 are hairline joints or point contacts (q2). The dashed circle marks the separate 1.03 ft opening that exists only at the +8 ft cut (q1d). A table under the map lists the coordinates, width and owners of all 16. White (non-green) floor such as 09-218 Student Commons is outside the current indoor envelope, which is the separate root cause in the routing report.

images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — 63.5 mm gap between a wall and a glass wall next to door #1948341
images.explanation: Room-scale view plus two zooms of the corner where the diagonal 100 mm wall #1521222 meets curtain-wall mullion #1948433 (host curtain wall #1948340, not an authoritative native owner) beside unmatched door #1948341. In the native model at 4 ft above Floor 0.5 the wall face and the mullion corner do not touch: the nearest points are 63.5 mm apart and the closing-disk test agrees (width class 0.207–0.211 ft). The registered DWG plan is continuous here: it draws a frame/mullion profile in this joint (parallel lines #1250/#1251, 0.368 ft long and 0.187 ft apart, plus many small profile lines), so on paper the corner is closed. The gap repeats at +8 ft (mullion #1948434). A provisional seal here would be an assumption; the native model itself leaves the gap.

images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — the '50 mm gap' by glass panel #1522657 is a mullion; the real leak is a hairline
images.explanation: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the report. At (286.52, 553.94) the evidence file's 'measured owner gap' of 50.0 mm is the distance from wall #1521392 to glass panel #1522657 measured straight across curtain mullion #1522662 (a 50 x 150 mm mullion), i.e. it is the mullion's width, and that space is filled by the mullion. The opening the enclosure test actually needs closed there is a hairline between the side of mullion #1522662 and the end face of wall #1521392: 5.3e-06 ft (0.0016 mm) at the mullion's corner, tapering to 2.7e-07 ft at its other corner. The closing-disk width class at this mouth is 0–0.0039 ft, which matches a hairline, not 50 mm. So this location belongs with the micro-gaps (q2), not with the real 63.5 mm / 11.9 mm gaps. The registered DWG facade line #421 (90 ft) is continuous here.

images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — 11.9 mm slot between wall #1521468 and glass-wall mullion #1521453
images.explanation: At the glass wall at y ≈ 461 (west part of the 09-201 corridor area), 90 mm wall #1521468 and curtain mullion #1521453 run side by side without touching, leaving a straight slot 11.9 mm wide and 0.49 ft long (y 461.06–461.56). The enclosure test leaks through it (closing-disk class 0.035–0.039 ft). Note the evidence file's automatic 'nearest owner pair' for this interval says 0 mm between #1521468 and #1521469 (those two walls touch elsewhere); the 11.9 mm was measured here directly between #1521468 and #1521453 and matches the report. The registered DWG wall line #3870 (16.4 ft) runs straight across the slot, so the paper plan shows the joint closed.

images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — 1.03 ft opening at 8 ft height where column #1521242 has no cut
images.explanation: At 8 ft above Floor 0.5 (and at +10 ft) the unchanged production cutter returns no closed cut for 400 mm column #1521242, although its source bounds run from -3.28 to 11.15 ft; at +0.1, +1 and +4 ft it is cut normally (dotted outline = its +4 ft cut). The existing user seal 1976247–1521242 (purple, 0.063 x 0.0035 ft) bridges the end of wall #1976247 to the column's corner, so at +8 ft it ends in empty space. The result is an opening between the seal's end and door #1975053 of about 1.03 ft (closing-disk class 1.031–1.039 ft; corner-to-corner 1.036 ft = 316 mm). Two smaller necessary intervals at +8 ft sit right next to it (0.12 ft at door #1975053 / wall #1521243 and 0.027 ft at wall #1976247 / the seal). The registered DWG draws the column outline (#439/#440/#441) and the facade line #2615 across this opening.

images.title: Building 9, Floor 0.5 — 13 micro-gaps (≤ 4.3 µm) that are invisible at normal drawing scale
images.explanation: Map of the 13 micro-gap intervals at the +4 ft cut (same numbering as q1-overview), with zoom panels A, C, D, E at about 0.7 m across — a normal close-up drawing scale — at a north-facade glass joint (#11) and at the jambs of doors #1521412 (#15), #1964672 (#4) and #1951047 (#16). At that scale every joint looks closed. The test still finds a passage at each, because the native bodies either touch only at a single point (width 0) or are separated by a hairline. Panel B magnifies joint #11 about 100,000 times to show the largest of the 13: 4.3 µm (1.4e-05 ft) between glass panel #1522624 and mullion #1522632. All 13 have closing-disk width class 0–0.0039 ft, and a registered DWG line lies within 0.11 ft of each. A generic exact-contact rule (treat sub-micrometre joints between curtain members, and between door frames and mullions, as closed) would close all of them; #7 from q1b is the same kind of hairline (1.6 µm).

items.owners: wall #1521392 / mullion #1522574 (no pair measured; point contact)

images.title: Building 9, Floor 2 — south facade (y ≈ 459): 8 openings of 0.9–2.6 ft where the model has no solid wall
images.explanation: On Floor 2 (level 694, cut at +4 ft) the south facade is modelled as walls #1521701 (x 184–248) and #1521704 (x 260–352). Both have reconstructed display geometry only (hatched); the native model has no body for them, so the enclosure cut holds only curtain mullions and glass (blue) and some interior walls. The test finds 8 necessary openings 0.92–2.63 ft wide on this facade (red bars, measured as straight-through gaps; they match the closing-disk width classes), plus 21 smaller necessary intervals. Four of the 8 sit exactly at native 400 mm columns #1521703/#1521705/#1521706/#1521707, whose source bounds span Floor 2 but which get no cut at any Floor 2 offset — the same symptom as q1d. The registered DWG facade line #710 is continuous for 95 ft (x 215.6–310.5, y ≈ 459.15). Correction to the report: the 3.8 ft opening is not on the south facade; it is on the north facade at (222.3, 550.4) beside reconstructed wall #1522479 (panel D).

measured.method: straight-through openings = x ranges where a vertical segment y 458.0–459.9 touches no barrier (cuts + door footprints/boxes + applied seals + frame returns), 0.005 ft sampling

images.title: Building 7/8, Floor 1.25 — unmatched door #1630256 between the ramp landing and stair 08-S101
images.explanation: The top of ramp #1622190 (node at 55.5, 466.5) and the 08-S101 stair hall are separated by a glazed diagonal wall (host #1629345). Door #1630256 (footprint 6.76 ft long, point 61.92, 464.61, normal pointing toward the stair hall) sits in that wall but is 'unmatched': its only owner is 08-S101, so no route is built through it. Routing cell 256 (orange) contains the ramp landing, the stair hall and office 08-106 together; inside it the landing reaches the stair hall only through a hairline of 2.3e-06 ft (0.0007 mm) at (71.46, 459.02) between a glazing hole and the wall — not walkable. Associating #1630256 as a two-owner door (landing ↔ 08-S101) would give the landing a real door to the stair hall and stair node. The registered DWG has frame profiles at both ends of the door span and no wall line across it (consistent with a doorway); there are no DWG door symbols in this DWG section near it. Separately, 08-102 Corridor has no routing cell, so door #2018182 (stair hall ↔ 08-102) is not attached either.

images.title: Building 7/8, Floor 1.25 — the 08-106 corner seam is a zero-width joint between two walls
images.explanation: Routing cell 256 joins office 08-106 to the stair hall through the joint between 08-106's east wall #2017986 and the diagonal wall #2017949 at the office's south-east corner. In the native plan cut the two walls share that edge exactly: it runs 1.97 ft (exactly 0.60 m) from (60.223, 471.295) to (61.207, 472.999), and the walls are 6e-15 ft apart (floating-point noise). The measured width of the seam is therefore 0 — there is no physical opening. The cell outline (orange line) runs into the joint and back out on the stair-hall side, which a pinch-aware test would not treat as a passage; eroding the cell by just 1e-9 ft already separates 08-106 from the stair hall. The registered DWG draws this corner closed (inner-face lines #1157/#1158 meet at 60.17, 471.21). So the seam looks like a cell-construction artefact rather than a real opening.
